title: People’s Mañanera November 24
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Mexico and China Strengthen Cooperation as They Approach 55 Years of
Diplomatic Relations  
** At the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, an agreement was
reached to establish a hospital in Mexico that will use AI to analyze CT scans
and speed up diagnoses, with medical validation. Cooperation in science,
energy, water, and tourism will be expanded. In addition, Xi Jinping will
consider the loan of a panda.

**Public Healthcare Strengthened: IMSS, ISSSTE, and IMSS-Bienestar Move
Forward with 12 Actions in 120 Days  
** “More equipment, permanent job status for sector employees, more staff, and
improved distribution of medications,” was how President Claudia Sheinbaum
described the latest advances in the Mexican healthcare system. The Mexican
Social Security Institute (IMSS) now has 4,119 facilities and 74 hospital
equipment units in operation. The Institute for Social Security and Services
for State Workers (ISSSTE) reached an 89% adoption rate for electronic
prescriptions, and IMSS-Bienestar opened a free hemodialysis center in Toluca.

**Mexico Posts 3.3% Annual Growth, Its Strongest Since 2023  
** “The economy is growing thanks to public work projects, housing, mixed
investments, and manufacturing,” Sheinbaum explained. She also anticipated a
new record for foreign direct investment.

**Election Material Contracts Must Be Investigated, and the Cost of Ballot
Boxes and Voting Booths Must Be Regulated  
** “A review must be conducted because this is the people’s money,” the
President stated. Sheinbaum called for continued investigation into why
contracts for the supply of election day materials were concentrated among
companies owned by the Hernández Casillas family. She noted that the National
Electoral Institute (INE) will have a budget of 36 billion pesos (US$1.88
billion) in 2027 and that it has the authority to regulate the prices of these
materials and foster competition among suppliers.
